chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Musa ibn Bakr, from Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him), who said:
When you pray Salat upon the woman, stand by her head; and when you pray Salat upon the man, stand by his chest.

key_terms.صَلَّيْتَ: You prayed (specifically Salat al-Janazah in this context)

ai.seo_question: Where should the Imam stand when leading funeral prayers for men and women?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi delineates the specific juristic positioning for the Imam during Salat al-Janazah, distinguishing between standing at the head for women and at the chest for men. This distinction reflects the scholarly consensus on the orientation of the deceased relative to the Qibla and the leader's proximity to the body's vital center, ensuring the ritual's validity and reverence.

en.hubeali:
A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Abu Nasr, from Musa Bin Bakr, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Al Hassan<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘When you pray Salaat upon the (deceased) woman, so stand by her head; and when you pray Salaat upon the man, so stand by his chest’.
en.sarwar: 2. A number of our people have narrated from Sahl ibn Ziyad from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn abu Nasr from Musa ibn Bakr who has said the following: “Abu al-Hassan ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘
When performing Salah (prayer) for a deceased woman you must stand up next to her head and for a man stand up next to his midsection.’”
